components.css: .ds-seg{display:inline-grid;grid-auto-flow:column;grid-auto-columns:1fr;background:rgba(118,118,128,.12);border-radius:9px;padding:2px;font-family:-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "SF Pro Text", system-ui, sans-serif}.ds-seg button{min-height:30px;padding:0 10px;border:0;background:none;border-radius:7px;font-size:13px;font-weight:500;cursor:pointer;color:inherit;white-space:nowrap}.ds-seg button[aria-checked="true"]{background:var(--seg-on,#fff);font-weight:600;box-shadow:0 3px 8px rgba(0,0,0,.12),0 3px 1px rgba(0,0,0,.04)}.ds-seg button:focus-visible{outline:2px solid #007AFF;outline-offset:2px}

components.name: Filter Chip
components.description: History category filter; the selected chip inverts to label fill.

components.name: Category Disc Picker
components.description: Category choice in the Add payment sheet; the chosen disc gets a double ring and the rest fade.
components.css: .ds-cats{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(4,1fr);gap:6px 4px;padding:12px;background:#F2F2F7;font-family:-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "SF Pro Text", system-ui, sans-serif}.ds-cat{display:flex;flex-direction:column;align-items:center;gap:5px;padding:6px 0 4px;border:0;background:none;border-radius:12px;font-size:12px;color:#000;cursor:pointer}.ds-disc{width:46px;height:46px;border-radius:50%;display:grid;place-items:center;background:var(--t);transition:transform .2s cubic-bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1),box-shadow .2s cubic-bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1),opacity .2s}.ds-cat:active .ds-disc{transform:scale(.92)}.ds-cat[aria-checked="false"] .ds-disc{opacity:.45}.ds-cat[aria-checked="true"]{font-weight:600}.ds-cat[aria-checked="true"] .ds-disc{box-shadow:0 0 0 2.5px #F2F2F7,0 0 0 5px var(--t)}.ds-cat:focus-visible{outline:2px solid #007AFF;outline-offset:2px}

components.name: Keypad
components.description: Custom amount keypad that replaces the system keyboard.
components.css: .ds-keypad{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(3,1fr);max-width:360px;background:#F2F2F7}.ds-keypad button{min-height:50px;border:0;background:none;border-radius:12px;font:400 28px -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "SF Pro Text", system-ui, sans-serif;font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums;display:grid;place-items:center;color:#000;cursor:pointer;transition:background .12s}.ds-keypad button:active{background:rgba(118,118,128,.2)}.ds-keypad button:focus-visible{outline:2px solid #007AFF;outline-offset:2px}

components.description: Undo toast after filing a payment.

narrative.overview:
Spending is meant to look like an app Apple ships, with no visual identity of its own. The owner chose standard iOS over a custom world, so the platform's conventions are the brand. It uses the system grouped background, inset rounded groups, the system font through Dynamic Type, system blue as the one tint, and system-palette colours for the eight categories. Things that would usually make an app distinctive, like an expressive typeface, an own palette, or decorative depth, are left out on purpose. The only additions are a bold Revolut-style total, a Health-style pace chart, and a hatched overshoot on budget meters.

The screens are dense but calm. Each screen leads with an iOS large title. Content sits in inset grouped lists with hairline separators. One prominent tint button is anchored in a translucent bottom toolbar, within thumb reach. Colour carries information. Category colour says which category a row is. Amber and red say how a budget is doing. Tint marks what you can tap. Light and dark modes follow the system and both are fully specified. Motion uses the iOS sheet curve.
keyCharacteristics: System grouped background with white (light) or #1C1C1E (dark) inset groups at a 12px radius.
System font via `-apple-system-body`. Every size is in rem, so the whole scale follows Dynamic Type.
Tabular numerals on every amount, axis label, count and keypad digit.
Category identity is a white glyph on a coloured 29px rounded tile in lists, and on a coloured disc in pickers.
Amber and red are the budget-state colours. Red also serves the iOS destructive role.
Translucent bar material only on the navbar once scrolled, the bottom toolbar, and the action sheet.

rules.name: The Reserved Status Rule
rules.body: Amber and red communicate budget state: near (≥80%) and over. Red also keeps its iOS meaning of destructive or error. Neither is ever used as a category colour, decoration or emphasis. A pace that is ahead but still within budget is shown in bold label colour, not amber.

rules.name: The One Tint Rule
rules.body: System blue is the only colour that means "tappable". Category colours never mark controls.

rules.name: The Dynamic Type Rule
rules.body: Every size is in rem off the `-apple-system-body` root. Never hard-code px for text, so the whole scale follows the user's text size setting.

rules.name: The Tabular Money Rule
rules.body: Every number that can change or line up with another (amounts, totals, counts, axis labels, keypad digits) uses `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`.

rules.name: The Flat Groups Rule
rules.body: Inset groups never get a shadow or border. They separate from the ground by tone alone.

dos: Do use the system tokens for every colour, and give each light value its iOS dark counterpart through `prefers-color-scheme`.
Do set every text size in rem off `-apple-system-body`, and use tabular numerals for all figures.
Do build lists as inset groups (12px radius) of rows at least 44px tall, with 0.5px separators inset to the text (16px, or 57px with a 29px tile).
Do keep the one prominent action as a 50px full-width tint button in the bottom toolbar or a sheet.
Do show overspend as a solid red bar plus a hatched excess segment, and near-budget as an amber fill.
Do move things with the iOS sheet curve, and drop to instant transitions under reduced motion.
donts: Don't use amber or red for anything except budget state, plus red for iOS destructive actions and errors. Never use them as a category colour or for emphasis.
Don't use any colour other than system blue for tappable controls.
Don't put shadows or borders on inset groups. Shadows are only for sheets, the selected segment and the toast.
Don't add a custom display face or a second font family. The system face is the identity.
Don't use system iOS red, orange or yellow as category colours.
